title: Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Counsel Underwriting, Retainer Economics, Evidence Provenance, Statutory Routing, Controlled Automation, and a Cash-Safe 30-Day Launch in Forensic Whistleblower Analytics

worksheets.title: Arbitrage Deal / Counterparty Underwriting & Spread Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Qualify a paying law-firm counterparty and a reproducible evidence thesis before spending scarce analyst hours. Separate a useful public-data anomaly from an actionable claim, document counsel's evidentiary requirements, and price support work independently of speculative statutory recoveries.
instructions: Start with one named counsel account, one dataset family, and one alleged payment mechanism. Record the purchasing decision-maker, retainer budget, conflict-screening method, and source permissions before compiling a subject-specific evidence package or circulating identifiable allegations.

Reproduce each anomaly against a defensible peer cohort and inspect ordinary explanations such as specialty, geography, coding changes, referral mix, and suppressed records. Treat statistical distance as a research lead rather than a finding of knowing misconduct.

Ask counsel to identify the government payment nexus, knowledge theory, materiality theory, and representative-claim requirements. Keep unavailable claim-level proof explicitly listed as an evidence gap; never manufacture patient records or imply aggregate utilization establishes false billing.

Create separate commercial and litigation decisions. A funded analytics assignment may proceed even when a statutory filing is unsuitable, provided the contract describes legitimate deliverables and prohibits contingent collection assumptions from funding current operating commitments.

Have counsel evaluate public disclosure, original-source status, first-to-file issues, and lawful evidence acquisition before selecting a filing route. Record rejection reasons and preservation instructions so an attractive anomaly does not bypass substantive eligibility screening.

fields.name: Paying counterparty and purchase authority
fields.prompt: Identify the law firm, authorized signer, billing contact, conflict-screening channel, and independent ability to pay. Specify a retainer purchase decision that does not depend on intervention, settlement, or award collection.
fields.example: Harbor Trial Group, a fictional plaintiff firm, authorizes a $7,500 monthly analytics retainer through its managing partner. Accounts payable accepts net-15 invoices. The engagement funds 45 analyst hours and one evidence memorandum monthly; payment remains due even if counsel declines every proposed statutory filing.

fields.name: Dataset thesis and government payment nexus
fields.prompt: Describe the source release, unit of observation, government payment relationship, and suspected mechanism. Distinguish provider-level aggregates from individual claims and explain what additional evidence would connect the anomaly to an actionable payment.
fields.example: The pilot compares one CMS Part B provider-service release with the matching Open Payments year. An orthopedic cohort contains 420 providers; 18 exceed the selected utilization threshold. The lead concerns potentially unsupported services, but aggregate payments establish neither an individual false claim nor knowledge of falsity.

fields.name: Peer cohort and innocent-explanation challenge
fields.prompt: Specify cohort inclusion rules, minimum sample size, normalization method, and alternative explanations. Record the analyst responsible for challenging the thesis and the result required before a subject enters counsel review.
fields.example: Compare providers within specialty and state, excluding cohorts below 30 members. A provider at 3.8 times median utilization falls to 1.4 times after site-of-service adjustment. The challenger removes that lead, retains the calculation, and prevents the original ranking from appearing in the counsel-facing priority queue.

fields.name: Representative-claim evidence sufficiency
fields.prompt: Ask counsel to map the applicable Rule 9(b) standard to available facts. Identify claim identifiers, dates, statements, payment evidence, and firsthand support while separating circuit-specific pleading requirements from internal research preferences.
fields.example: Counsel requests two lawfully obtained representative transactions showing service date, billing code, asserted falsity, and payment connection. The public dataset supplies none of those complete transactions. The evidence matrix therefore records an unresolved pleading gap, assigns counsel to assess permissible alternatives, and prevents an analyst from labeling the matter filing-ready.

fields.name: Public-disclosure and original-source screen
fields.prompt: Inventory earlier reports, proceedings, media coverage, and government disclosures relevant to substantially the same allegations. Have counsel assess 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), including applicable disclosure categories and original-source facts.
fields.example: A trade article already describes the same billing pattern, and the analyst used only published aggregates. Counsel records elevated public-disclosure risk and requests evidence of qualifying independent knowledge that materially adds to the disclosure. The team does not assume that downloading government data automatically establishes or defeats original-source status.

fields.name: First-to-file, conflicts, and relator identity
fields.prompt: Record counsel's conflict result, proposed relator identity, overlapping public litigation, and limits on discovering sealed cases. Separate entity matching from legal conclusions about 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(5) and relator eligibility.
fields.example: The conflict screen clears the fictional purchasing firm for an initial engagement. Counsel identifies one public related action but cannot exclude an earlier sealed complaint. The proposed relator's knowledge chronology remains separate from the analytics company's service contract; a data vendor is not automatically the proper statutory claimant.

fields.name: Retainer scope and contribution spread
fields.prompt: Define deliverable limits, included hours, contractor rates, revision allowances, and direct delivery costs. Calculate assignment contribution before shared overhead and owner profit; exclude hypothetical government recoveries from the commercial spread calculation.
fields.example: A $7,500 monthly retainer includes 45 hours at $70 internal delivery cost, $300 source processing, and $550 independent review. Direct cost totals $4,000; assignment contribution is $3,500, or 46.67%. This assignment spread excludes shared overhead and does not replace the canonical 45.0% Base annual net margin.

fields.name: Authorized evidence boundary and access record
fields.prompt: List permitted public sources, licensed datasets, client-provided materials, and restricted categories. Require written authority for nonpublic records and distinguish lawful preservation from unauthorized access, credential sharing, or acquisition of privileged third-party communications.
fields.example: The engagement permits CMS downloads, SAM.gov public notices, licensed import-manifest records, and documents counsel lawfully supplies. It excludes hospital credentials, patient portal access, and employer mailbox exports without established authority. Sensitive source material enters a restricted workspace only after counsel documents acquisition rights and the assigned analyst's access.

fields.name: Lead disposition and commercial decision
fields.prompt: Set separate acceptance criteria for paid research and potential litigation. Record evidence gaps, maximum research spend, decision owner, and expiration date so an unresolved legal thesis cannot silently become an unlimited unpaid investigation.
fields.example: Counsel purchases a $3,000 fixed-scope corroboration memo despite unresolved claim-level evidence. Work stops after 20 analyst hours or delivery, whichever occurs first under the agreed scope. Filing consideration remains deferred until counsel resolves eligibility and pleading issues; the vendor's invoice is payable regardless of that decision.

fields.name: Zero-recovery underwriting and concentration limit
fields.prompt: Test the account assuming every proposed matter yields no award. Identify retainer collection risk, client concentration, termination exposure, and the cash-funded workload that remains supportable without settlement proceeds or advances against contingent claims.
fields.example: The first firm represents 100% of initial revenue, so contractors receive only funded monthly assignments. The downside model sets all statutory receipts to $0 for five years. A 30-day termination clause triggers scope reduction rather than borrowing against a sealed matter or promising contractors a future recovery.

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance only when a named firm can fund the defined scope, counsel has documented eligibility and evidence gaps, and the engagement remains viable with every statutory award receipt set to $0.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Escrow/Reserve Float & Working-Capital Calculator
worksheets.purpose: Build a cash model that survives lengthy investigations and complete recovery failure. Reconcile all three canonical annual scenarios, distinguish earned service revenue from collected cash, and keep restricted funds, claim values, government collections, and contingent award interests outside spendable runway.
instructions: Copy the canonical annual revenue, margin, profit, and staffing figures without substituting a probability-weighted recovery forecast. Build a service-revenue bridge capable of supporting each scenario, and label that bridge as a planning composition rather than historical performance.

Separate signed contracts, earned revenue, invoices, collections, restricted cash, and award contingencies into distinct accounts. Apply contract-specific recognition treatment and have the accountant resolve ASC 606 principal-agent questions before presenting gross amounts as operator revenue.

Calculate monthly cash commitments from actual staffing and payment terms. Keep the stated overhead range separate from total delivery costs, and recognize that a funded launch budget can still expire before the four-to-twelve-month first-deal window closes.

Model non-intervention, dismissal, settlement delay, unsuccessful proceedings, and collection delay explicitly. Use documented cohort denominators for observed rates; label planning assumptions clearly instead of presenting a selected dismissal percentage as a universal government statistic.

Reconcile every reserve movement to an unrestricted bank balance and a written release condition. Do not treat client trust funds, refundable advances, government recovery principal, or a projected relator share as freely available operating float.

fields.name: Conservative scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter the exact Conservative revenue, net margin, owner profit, and team. Provide a service-only revenue bridge and implied annual costs, preserving the distinction between canonical outputs and an illustrative sales mix.
fields.example: Conservative revenue is $95,000 with a 32% net margin and $30,400 annual owner net profit; team capacity is 1 FT + 2 C. An illustrative bridge is $6,000 monthly retainers for 12 months plus $23,000 project fees. Implied total annual costs are $64,600; award receipts are $0.

fields.name: Base scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter the exact Base revenue, net margin, owner profit, and team. Reconcile a complete annual delivery-cost envelope and a repeatable retainer mix without adding contingent recoveries to recognized service revenue.
fields.example: Base revenue is $487,500, margin is 45.0%, and annual owner net profit is $219,375 with 1 FT + 2 C. Five $7,500 monthly retainers generate $450,000; projects add $37,500. Costs total $268,125, comprising $72,000 overhead, $144,000 delivery labor, $36,000 project costs, and $16,125 administration.

fields.name: Scaled Small-Team scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter the exact Scaled revenue, net margin, owner profit, and staffing. Identify the capacity assumptions supporting higher contribution, and calculate implied costs without extending the scenario beyond the specified five-person team.
fields.example: Scaled revenue is $880,000 at 58% net margin, producing $510,400 annual owner net profit with 2 FT + 3 C, five people total. Eight $8,750 monthly retainers generate $840,000; projects add $40,000. Implied costs are $369,600, requiring reusable pipelines and measured delivery efficiency rather than assumed award proceeds.

fields.name: Recognized revenue and retained-share boundary
fields.prompt: Distinguish gross service billings, pass-through amounts, government collections, statutory awards, and the operator's legally attributable interest. Document ASC 606 principal-agent treatment for service contracts and the accountant's separate treatment of any award.
fields.example: A fictional matter produces $10 million in government collections, but the operator records none of that principal as revenue. A $40,000 research assignment contains $10,000 of agent-arranged pass-through services; under the assumed net presentation, service revenue is $30,000 and retained_share equals 0.75. Statutory receipts remain separately evaluated.

fields.name: Monthly overhead and full operating commitment
fields.prompt: Identify recurring overhead within the stated $1,500–$9,500 range, then add labor, delivery, and administrative obligations separately. Explain which commitments activate only after collections and which continue during a client acquisition drought.
fields.example: Base overhead is $6,000 monthly, within the stated range. Allocated labor is $12,000, project costs average $3,000, and administration averages $1,343.75, producing total monthly costs of $22,343.75. Average Base revenue is $40,625 monthly. These annualized allocations describe steady-state operations, not the initial pre-client burn.

fields.name: Startup capital and first-deal runway
fields.prompt: Select startup capital within $10,000–$45,000 and deduct one-time launch spending. Calculate pre-client runway against the four-to-twelve-month first-deal range, including a concrete cost reduction when the initial funding cannot cover that interval.
fields.example: Starting capital of $30,000 less $6,000 setup leaves $24,000. At $6,000 monthly pre-client burn, runway is four months, leaving an eight-month gap against a twelve-month first deal. Reducing committed burn to $2,000 extends runway to twelve months; paid contractors begin only after funded client work arrives.

fields.name: Restricted advances and reserve release
fields.prompt: Separate vendor advances, counsel-controlled trust funds, refundable balances, and unrestricted reserves. Specify ownership, refund duties, recognition timing, and release conditions rather than treating all deposited funds as productive operating capital.
fields.example: A firm pays a $15,000 advance covering two future service months. The ledger initially records a contract liability, subject to the actual cancellation terms. The operator excludes the refundable balance from discretionary reserves. Counsel's client trust account remains outside operator custody, and no interest benefit is assumed.

fields.name: Collections lag and working-capital stress
fields.prompt: Calculate the cash gap caused by delayed invoices using full operating commitments rather than overhead alone. Identify minimum unrestricted cash, contractor payment dates, receivable aging triggers, and a specific stop-work response.
fields.example: At Base monthly costs of $22,343.75, a conservative two-month collection interruption requires $44,687.50 before any incremental project spending. A $50,000 unrestricted reserve leaves $5,312.50 above that stress requirement. Invoices exceeding 30 days trigger partner outreach; new unfunded deliverables pause under the engagement's agreed suspension clause.

fields.name: Non-intervention, dismissal, and zero-recovery tree
fields.prompt: Build a complete outcome tree with explicit denominators for non-intervention and dismissal rates. Treat Granston-era dismissal policy as context, not a universal rate, and distinguish screening assumptions from observed case outcomes.
fields.example: An illustrative 100-filed-matter stress cohort assumes 80 non-interventions. Within those 80, eight dismissals imply 10%; 60 other matters yield no recovery and 12 recover. Of 20 intervention matters, four yield zero and 16 recover. Total zero-recovery outcomes are 72; these are scenario assumptions, not published DOJ frequencies.

fields.name: Award timing and cash exclusion schedule
fields.prompt: Maintain a separate contingent-upside schedule showing route, statutory range, counsel assessment, expected delay, and collection status. Exclude uncollected awards from payroll coverage, operating reserves, canonical revenue bridges, and debt service calculations.
fields.example: The upside schedule assumes potential realization in years two through five or later, with FCA investigations potentially remaining under extended seal. All five annual operating budgets assign uncollected awards $0 spendable cash. SEC and IRS matters follow their own confidentiality regimes rather than being described as FCA sealed dockets.

worksheets.completion_gate: Approve the model only when all three canonical profits reconcile exactly, restricted balances are excluded from runway, and both the launch plan and steady-state commitments survive the stated zero-award cash stress.

worksheets.title: End-to-End Execution, Idempotent Ledger & QA Pre-Flight Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Turn an authorized research assignment into a reproducible, counsel-ready evidence package without corrupting provenance or leaking restricted facts. Define immutable acquisition records, reversible transformations, duplicate controls, human verification, and invoice events that survive reruns and independent reconstruction.
instructions: Assign a non-descriptive matter identifier before acquisition, then record the source release, retrieval time, authority, checksum, and custodian. Preserve source bytes separately from normalized working copies so later transformations never overwrite the original evidence.

Run ingestion and entity resolution with stable keys and explicit versioning. Treat repeat delivery as a replay, not a new business event. Quarantine schema changes and unresolved identifiers before they affect rankings, evidence exports, or invoices.

Make every allegation traceable to source records and every calculation reproducible from a recorded configuration. Keep analyst interpretation visibly separate from source text, and require a second person to challenge material factual assertions.

Use restricted workspaces for counsel-controlled material and segregate ordinary sales records from matter evidence. Before transmission, verify recipients, authorization, export contents, and attachment metadata; avoid external processing services unless the engagement specifically permits them.

Close delivery only after artifact counts, hashes, claim references, permissions, and commercial milestones reconcile. Record failed checks as open work rather than silently repairing the evidence history or marking an incomplete package as accepted.

fields.name: Matter identifier and authorization envelope
fields.prompt: Assign a stable opaque matter identifier and capture who authorized research, permitted sources, data classes, workspace members, and delivery scope. Keep subject names and allegation language out of broadly visible project identifiers.
fields.example: Matter M048-001 covers a 20-hour public-source corroboration assignment authorized by counsel's engagement email. Workspace access includes one lead analyst, one reviewer, and two designated firm contacts. The sales board contains only M048-001 and contract value; it contains no subject identity, allegations, or sealed-case status.

fields.name: Acquisition manifest and source integrity
fields.prompt: Record retrieval timestamp, source URL or licensed delivery reference, release identifier, byte count, checksum algorithm, and acquisition authority. Explain how replacement releases are preserved without erasing earlier source versions.
fields.example: The manifest records a CMS release downloaded at 14:20 UTC, its published release label, 184,320,000 bytes, and the full machine-generated SHA-256 digest in a dedicated checksum field. A corrected release receives a second immutable artifact identifier; the original remains available with its superseded status and retrieval history.

fields.name: Normalization specification and excluded records
fields.prompt: Document column mappings, types, suppression handling, units, rounding, and exclusion reasons. Identify source changes that stop processing rather than allowing coercion to create misleading zeros or silently shift monetary scales.
fields.example: The parser stores payment amounts as integer cents and provider identifiers as strings. Suppressed counts remain explicitly suppressed rather than becoming zero. Of 120,000 rows, 350 missing stable identifiers enter quarantine. A changed payment-column name stops the run until the reviewer approves a versioned mapping update.

fields.name: Entity resolution and collision handling
fields.prompt: Specify authoritative identifiers, match precedence, temporal validity, and collision handling across CMS, Open Payments, procurement, and manifests. Prevent name similarity alone from combining unrelated organizations or assigning conduct to the wrong person.
fields.example: CMS records join through validated NPI values where appropriate; procurement entities use UEI and documented historical crosswalks. Two similarly named importers share no verified identifier, so they remain separate. A reviewer resolves 12 candidate matches and rejects five; rejected pairs persist in a versioned do-not-merge register.

fields.name: Idempotent event and artifact ledger
fields.prompt: Define stable deduplication keys, transaction boundaries, retry behavior, and immutable event references. Explain how repeated ingestion, delivery acknowledgments, or invoice requests avoid duplicate evidence records and duplicate commercial charges.
fields.example: A SQLite ledger enforces a unique tuple of matter identifier, source release, source-record key, and transformation version. Replaying 5,000 previously processed records inserts zero duplicates. Invoice events use a separate unique matter-period-milestone key; a retried delivery acknowledgment references the original event instead of generating a second bill.

fields.name: Anomaly reproducibility and negative controls
fields.prompt: Capture scoring parameters, cohort membership, software version, random seed where used, and negative-control outcomes. Require explanations for unstable rankings before an anomaly is represented as a priority investigative lead.
fields.example: Model version 1.3 ranks 420 providers using specialty-adjusted service intensity. A shuffled-provider negative control produces no stable priority cluster. Changing the minimum cohort from 30 to 40 removes three of 18 leads; the memo reports that sensitivity and preserves both output manifests for review.

fields.name: Evidence assertion and contradiction matrix
fields.prompt: Link each material assertion to exact source locations, supporting records, contradictory evidence, and reviewer disposition. Distinguish verbatim source content, computed findings, witness statements, and counsel's legal analysis in the delivered package.
fields.example: Assertion A-07 reports unusually high service intensity and cites source rows 1842–1859 plus calculation C-14. A public specialty description supplies a plausible alternative explanation. The reviewer changes the conclusion from suspected false billing to unresolved utilization anomaly and assigns counsel a targeted corroboration question.

fields.name: Restricted export and recipient verification
fields.prompt: List export recipients, counsel authorization, encryption method, attachment inventory, redaction checks, and access expiration. Specify the conditions that stop delivery when a package contains seal-sensitive or improperly scoped material.
fields.example: Package P-004 contains one memo and three evidence appendices. Counsel confirms two named recipients through the existing engagement channel. The reviewer removes internal subject aliases from document properties, verifies redactions, and sets seven-day access expiry. A mismatched recipient address stops transmission until independently corrected.

fields.name: Delivery acceptance and invoice reconciliation
fields.prompt: Connect contract milestones to accepted artifacts, invoice amounts, revenue treatment, and collection status. Separate evidence revisions from new paid scope so a rerun or corrected file cannot accidentally create additional billable events.
fields.example: The monthly contract requires one memo and one counsel review call for $7,500. Acceptance event D-011 references the artifact manifest and meeting record. A corrected appendix replaces the deliverable version without changing the milestone key. Invoice I-011 remains $7,500, with collection tracked separately from delivery acceptance.

fields.name: Failed-check register and recovery rehearsal
fields.prompt: Record blocking defects, severity, owner, correction evidence, and rerun results. Include a restoration rehearsal demonstrating that evidence, ledger uniqueness, and access restrictions survive a failed job or workstation loss.
fields.example: A checksum mismatch blocks one downloaded archive and every dependent output. The operator retrieves a fresh authorized copy, preserves the failed acquisition record, and reruns processing. A separate restore test rebuilds 24 artifacts from backup with matching hashes and confirms that replay creates no duplicate invoices.

worksheets.completion_gate: Release the package only after provenance, entity matching, assertions, recipient authorization, duplicate prevention, and invoice totals pass documented checks; every remaining evidentiary limitation must appear in the counsel-facing delivery record.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract Addendum & Compliance Audit
worksheets.purpose: Translate statutory routes and professional boundaries into concrete operating controls. Reserve legal judgments and filings for licensed counsel, preserve FCA seal procedures, distinguish award programs accurately, and prevent service contracts from implying transferable awards, protected status, or permission to acquire restricted evidence.
instructions: Assign licensed counsel to select the cause of action, claimant, forum, filing sequence, and required disclosures. The analytics team supplies verified factual work and source records; it does not independently file complaints or represent a relator.

For an FCA route, document statutory eligibility, first-to-file exposure, pleading sufficiency, service requirements, and seal instructions. Treat the statutory initial seal period and every court extension as active handling requirements rather than a marketing timeline.

For SEC, IRS, or CFTC routes, create separate eligibility and submission checklists. Do not transfer FCA award percentages, seal procedures, or originality standards across programs; have counsel verify the governing provisions and current official forms.

Review engagement language for unauthorized legal practice, professional fee-sharing restrictions, evidence ownership, confidentiality, access rights, and refund duties. Specify fixed or hourly analytics compensation without assuming a vendor may purchase a statutory award interest.

Recheck current statutes, regulations, court orders, and local professional rules before each filing or sensitive disclosure. Record the authority consulted, reviewing lawyer, unresolved issue, and required operational restriction instead of relying on a generic certification.

fields.name: Licensed counsel and reserved decisions
fields.prompt: Identify counsel's licensed jurisdiction, engagement scope, filing responsibility, and escalation contact. List the legal determinations reserved to counsel and the factual services the analytics operator may deliver under the signed engagement.
fields.example: The engagement assigns counsel responsibility for claimant eligibility, causes of action, pleading, filing, service, and communications with agencies. The operator prepares reproducible calculations and source indexes for $7,500 monthly. Counsel verifies applicable admission requirements before litigation; the vendor does not describe its analysts as legal representatives.

fields.name: FCA seal, filing, and government service
fields.prompt: Translate 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2) into a counsel-owned filing checklist. Include in-camera filing, initial seal duration, government service materials, defendant-service restrictions, and controls for court-ordered extensions and disclosure permissions.
fields.example: Counsel files the complaint in camera and under seal for at least 60 days, serving the government with the complaint and substantially all material evidence and information as required. The defendant is not served until the court orders. Analysts follow each extension order and make no public case announcement.

fields.name: Public disclosure, first-to-file, and particularity
fields.prompt: Record counsel's analysis under 31 U.S.C. §§ 3730(e)(4) and 3730(b)(5), plus Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b). Identify unresolved factual gaps and jurisdiction-specific pleading standards without reducing eligibility to a dataset originality score.
fields.example: Counsel finds that an earlier news report may disclose substantially the same allegations, while the proposed relator has no documented qualifying original-source contribution. Representative transactions also remain missing. The matter receives a hold on filing work, a lawful corroboration plan, and a capped research budget rather than an eligibility certificate.

fields.name: FCA award range and dismissal exposure
fields.prompt: Distinguish intervened and non-intervened FCA award ranges and record exclusions, reductions, government dismissal authority, and court-dependent seal consequences. Do not promise an award percentage or describe every seal violation as automatic forfeiture.
fields.example: Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(d), ordinary ranges are 15%–25% when the government proceeds and 25%–30% when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications. Counsel separately assesses dismissal under § 3730(c)(2)(A), including applicable Polansky procedures. Seal breaches can cause serious sanctions and case loss; consequences depend on governing law and facts.

fields.name: SEC Form TCR and award eligibility
fields.prompt: Document counsel's SEC submission route, original-information analysis, voluntary-submission timing, monetary threshold, and award-application tracking. Distinguish independent analysis eligibility from assumptions that any public-data ranking earns a statutory award.
fields.example: Counsel evaluates a proposed Form TCR under 15 U.S.C. § 78u-6 and 17 CFR §§ 240.21F-2 through 240.21F-4. Covered actions generally require sanctions exceeding $1 million; potential awards are 10%–30% of qualifying collections. The file records originality, exclusions, submission timing, and the later award-claim deadline as separate issues.

fields.name: IRS Form 211 threshold and evidence routing
fields.prompt: Record the taxpayer nexus, evidence of underpayment, amount-in-dispute analysis, individual income threshold where relevant, and counsel's Form 211 preparation plan. Distinguish mandatory-program eligibility from discretionary awards and eventual proceeds collection.
fields.example: Counsel evaluates 26 U.S.C. § 7623(b), whose 15%–30% framework generally requires proceeds in dispute exceeding $2 million. For an individual taxpayer, gross income must exceed $200,000 for a relevant taxable year. The operator supplies lawfully sourced transaction analysis; counsel prepares Form 211 and evaluates reductions or alternate treatment.

fields.name: CFTC route and cross-program separation
fields.prompt: Where derivatives conduct is relevant, record counsel's CFTC route under its distinct statute and regulations. Separate agency jurisdiction, submission records, related-action treatment, confidentiality instructions, and award calculations from FCA, SEC, and IRS assumptions.
fields.example: A derivatives-manipulation lead goes to counsel for analysis under 7 U.S.C. § 26 and 17 CFR Part 165. The CFTC framework generally uses a sanctions threshold exceeding $1 million and a 10%–30% award range. A separate submission register prevents treating one factual package as automatically eligible across agencies.

fields.name: Compensation addendum and award-interest restriction
fields.prompt: Draft concrete compensation terms covering service fees, pass-through expenses, contingent interests, and professional-rule review. Require counsel to assess applicable state fee-sharing and unauthorized-practice rules before any proposed recovery-linked arrangement.
fields.example: The addendum states: 'Analytics fees are $7,500 monthly for the defined services and are payable independently of litigation outcomes. This agreement assigns no statutory award and no legal-fee interest.' Counsel reviews applicable state rules corresponding to professional-conduct Rule 5.4 before considering any different compensation structure.

fields.name: Evidence access, privacy, and reporting rights
fields.prompt: Identify lawful collection authority, sensitive-data restrictions, protective orders, privilege handling, and reporting-rights language. Avoid treating an engagement or confidentiality clause as permission to access unrelated systems or impede protected agency communications.
fields.example: Counsel limits the pilot to public and licensed data, with no patient-level protected information. Any later health-data work requires a documented HIPAA analysis under 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164. The confidentiality addendum preserves applicable reporting rights and is reviewed against SEC Rule 21F-17's anti-impeding requirements.

fields.name: Seal incident and preservation response
fields.prompt: Define immediate steps for suspected disclosure, misdirected transmission, or unauthorized access. Preserve evidence, restrict further dissemination, notify counsel, and reserve court or agency communications for the responsible lawyer under applicable duties.
fields.example: An analyst discovers that a restricted attachment went to an unintended recipient. They disable the access link, preserve the message and access log, and immediately notify counsel. Counsel determines required court action and recipient instructions. The operator neither deletes the audit trail nor publicly explains the underlying sealed allegations.

worksheets.completion_gate: Proceed only with counsel-owned filing instructions, documented program eligibility analysis, enforceable service terms, and a tested restricted disclosure response; unresolved legal questions remain assigned to counsel with explicit work limits.

worksheets.title: Automation Pipeline, Acquisition Flywheel & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate repeatable acquisition, normalization, and evidence assembly while keeping legal conclusions and sensitive disclosures under human control. Build a counsel acquisition loop using sanitized capability demonstrations, measure useful output rather than lead volume, and define practical fallbacks for source failures.
instructions: Prioritize one reproducible pipeline before adding more datasets. Use authorized APIs or published downloads, documented rate limits, stable source versions, and bounded retry behavior so automation improves evidence quality instead of amplifying acquisition mistakes.

Separate deterministic calculations from interpretive drafting. Require source citations and reviewer approval for every material assertion, and prohibit automated filing, subject contact, or public accusation based solely on an anomaly score or generated summary.

Use public or synthetic examples to demonstrate capability to prospective firms. Track permission to contact, qualified meetings, paid pilots, retainer conversion, and collection timing without exposing sealed matters or promising recoveries as a sales tactic.

Define fallback behavior for unavailable sources, schema drift, excessive false positives, client loss, and counsel rejection. Every fallback must state an owner, spending ceiling, maximum delay, and the condition for resuming ordinary production.

Review automation performance alongside evidence accuracy and security events. Retire a pipeline when repeated errors consume its claimed labor savings, and preserve a manual route capable of delivering the contracted memo without unsupported technical shortcuts.

fields.name: Authorized source schedule and retry budget
fields.prompt: List CMS, Open Payments, SAM.gov, and licensed manifest acquisition schedules with access authority and release cadence. Set timeouts, rate limits, retry ceilings, and ownership for failed or changed source deliveries.
fields.example: The operator checks CMS and Open Payments release notices weekly, retrieves SAM.gov records through authorized access, and imports manifests under a commercial license. Each job allows three bounded retries before pausing. The lead analyst reviews failures the next business day; no job bypasses access restrictions to maintain freshness.

fields.name: Stdlib pipeline components and handoff contracts
fields.prompt: Define small ingestion, validation, scoring, ledger, and export components with explicit inputs and outputs. Specify the minimal Python standard-library implementation and the checks required before each component hands data to the next.
fields.example: The prototype uses urllib.request for authorized retrieval, csv and json for parsing, decimal for money, hashlib for checksums, and sqlite3 for event storage. Each component emits a manifest containing version, row counts, and rejection counts. The export component accepts only reviewed evidence assertions.

fields.name: Outlier precision and research-hour yield
fields.prompt: Measure counsel-useful leads against reviewed candidates, including false positives and hours spent. Define an economic threshold for retaining a scoring rule rather than optimizing for the largest possible anomaly queue.
fields.example: A batch produces 40 candidates; human review finds eight sufficiently corroborated for counsel discussion, a 20% useful-lead rate. Review takes 24 hours, or three hours per useful lead. A revised cohort rule produces six useful leads in 12 hours, improving yield despite lower headline candidate volume.

fields.name: FOIA and primary-source corroboration queue
fields.prompt: Track targeted public-record requests, custodian, statutory route, expected limitations, fees, and fallback sources. Keep FOIA response timing separate from contractual delivery promises and protect restricted matter details in request language.
fields.example: Counsel approves a narrowly scoped request under 5 U.S.C. § 552 for identified contract-payment records, with a $250 fee ceiling. The queue anticipates redactions and delays, including potential Exemptions 4, 6, or 7. The current paid memo proceeds using available primary records and explicitly lists missing corroboration.

fields.name: Dossier assembly and assertion review
fields.prompt: Specify which dossier sections can be assembled automatically and which require analyst or counsel judgment. Require precise citations, contradiction handling, and reproducibility before generated narrative reaches an external recipient.
fields.example: Automation assembles source inventories, entity crosswalks, calculation tables, and evidence references. The analyst writes factual interpretation and the reviewer checks every material sentence against cited artifacts. Counsel alone supplies legal theories. A missing citation blocks that assertion from the export, not merely from a footnote list.

fields.name: Counsel acquisition funnel and paid-pilot offer
fields.prompt: Define the target firm profile, permitted outreach channel, sanitized demonstration, paid pilot scope, and conversion metric. Separate historical conversion observations from launch assumptions and avoid subject-specific allegations in prospecting.
fields.example: The launch targets 30 firms with relevant public practice profiles through individualized business outreach. Planning assumptions are six meetings, two $3,000 paid pilots, and one retainer discussion. The demonstration uses synthetic entities and public methodology. These funnel counts are targets, not reported sales or expected award outcomes.

fields.name: Reuse, confidentiality, and referral flywheel
fields.prompt: Identify reusable methods, client-owned deliverables, restricted evidence, and permitted case-study content. Define how satisfied clients may introduce other firms without sharing protected matter details or creating unreviewed compensation obligations.
fields.example: After an accepted pilot, the firm may introduce the operator to another practice partner using a generic capability statement. No referral payment is offered. Reusable parsing code remains separate from client evidence, and the operator publishes neither subject names nor matter outcomes without documented authority and counsel review.

fields.name: Seal-sensitive tooling and third-party boundaries
fields.prompt: Document where restricted data may be processed, which external services are authorized, retention settings, access logs, and incident ownership. Treat uploading client material as a disclosure decision rather than a routine formatting operation.
fields.example: Restricted documents remain in the counsel-approved workspace with named-user access and logged exports. Public demonstrations run separately. Analysts do not upload matter text to external drafting services. Any proposed service requires documented client authority, reviewed retention terms, and a tested deletion and incident-response procedure.

fields.name: Source outage and quality fallback
fields.prompt: Define fallback sources, maximum stale-data age, manual review scope, spending cap, and client communication for a failed source or deteriorating model. Prohibit silent substitution of incomplete or incompatible releases.
fields.example: If the current CMS download fails validation, the analyst may use the prior verified release only with its date prominently stated and counsel's scope agreement. Manual triage is capped at six hours and $420 internal cost. New comparisons spanning incompatible release definitions remain paused.

fields.name: Automation return and retirement trigger
fields.prompt: Compare build effort, maintenance, verification, and avoided labor using the same cost basis. Define the error threshold and payback horizon that justify maintaining, revising, or retiring an automated component.
fields.example: A dossier assembler costs 40 hours at $70, or $2,800, to build. It saves ten monthly hours but requires two maintenance hours, yielding $560 monthly net labor savings and five-month payback. Two material citation errors in one month trigger manual assembly until the defect is resolved.

worksheets.completion_gate: Scale automation only after a reproducible pilot demonstrates useful lead yield, controlled disclosures, positive measured labor economics, and a funded manual fallback; outreach must use authorized, nonrestricted demonstration material.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Convert the operating model into a funded first-month sprint with accountable owners and measurable evidence quality. Track retainer collections, capacity, runway, and client concentration while preparing transferable business records that exclude restricted case materials and speculative valuations of uncollected awards.
instructions: Treat the first 30 days as infrastructure, validation, and commercial discovery rather than a promise of a closed engagement. Preserve the four-to-twelve-month first-deal assumption and fund only work that fits the current unrestricted launch reserve.

Assign one accountable owner to each deliverable, review task, and cash decision. Translate the canonical staffing labels into funded capacity and actual contractor commitments; do not assume a contractor count represents unlimited or full-time availability.

Publish a weekly scorecard separating activity, quality, commercial conversion, earned revenue, collections, and cash runway. Count a metric only when its supporting artifact exists, and mark missed targets as missed rather than redefining success.

Prepare an exit ledger that distinguishes owned software, reusable methods, assignable contracts, restricted client materials, and contingent personal rights. Require counsel review before buyer disclosure or transfer, and do not assume statutory interests are saleable business assets.

End the sprint with an evidence-based continue, narrow, or pause decision. Keep the canonical annual scenarios as planning benchmarks while using actual collections, delivery capacity, and source quality to determine the next month's authorized spending.

fields.name: Days 1–7 foundation and spending ceiling
fields.prompt: Set first-week deliverables for engagement design, counsel review, source selection, workspace setup, and budget controls. Identify the owner and acceptance artifact for each item without assuming an immediate paying client.
fields.example: The founder owns a one-source pilot specification, draft service agreement, and $30,000 capital ledger. Week-one spending is capped at $2,500 within the $6,000 setup allowance. Acceptance requires a counsel-reviewed scope, authorized source record, and restricted workspace test, not a completed filing or signed retainer.

fields.name: Days 8–14 reproducible demonstration
fields.prompt: Define a narrow demonstration dataset, reproducibility test, independent challenge, and sanitized presentation. Specify what counts as a usable capability demonstration while preventing unverified public allegations or unauthorized disclosures.
fields.example: The analyst builds one CMS cohort using synthetic subject labels in the external presentation. A contractor receives six funded review hours to challenge normalization and alternative explanations. Success means identical rerun outputs, traceable calculations, and a sanitized methodology memo; it does not mean identifying fraud.

fields.name: Days 15–21 counsel discovery and pilot scope
fields.prompt: Set targeted outreach, meeting, and proposal goals with a defined paid deliverable. Capture buyer objections and budget evidence without converting informal interest into booked revenue or a forecast award.
fields.example: The founder contacts 15 selected firms and seeks three discovery meetings. The proposed pilot costs $3,000 for a capped 20-hour corroboration memo. Meeting notes record practice fit, purchasing authority, and evidence requirements. An interested partner without a signed scope remains a prospect, with $0 earned revenue.

fields.name: Days 22–30 acceptance and next-month decision
fields.prompt: List month-end artifacts, unresolved defects, commercial results, and cash remaining. Define the conditions for continuing outreach, narrowing the offer, or pausing spend when the launch has not produced a contract.
fields.example: At day 30, the operator has one validated demonstration, four counsel meetings, and no signed pilot. With $22,000 remaining after $6,000 setup and $2,000 operating spend, they continue targeted outreach at the $2,000 monthly ceiling. The result is launch readiness, not a completed first deal.

fields.name: Pod roles and funded delivery capacity
fields.prompt: Translate 1 FT + 2 C and 2 FT + 3 C into responsibilities, available hours, review coverage, and funded commitments. Distinguish roster membership from actual billable availability before accepting additional retainers.
fields.example: The Base pod assigns the founder 100 monthly delivery hours and two contractors 80 hours each, totaling 260. Five retainers at 45 hours consume 225, leaving 35 for projects and review. Any proposal exceeding that capacity requires reduced scope or funded capacity before acceptance.

fields.name: Weekly cash and acquisition KPI scorecard
fields.prompt: Define exact numerators, denominators, data sources, and owners for acquisition, retention, collections, and runway metrics. Keep signed contract value, earned revenue, and banked cash separate in every weekly review.
fields.example: Week four records 30 outreach attempts, six meetings, two proposals, and zero signed engagements. Meeting conversion is 20%; proposal conversion from meetings is 33.33%. Earned service revenue and collections both remain $0. The founder reconciles runway to the bank ledger rather than pipeline value.

fields.name: Evidence quality and adverse-outcome scorecard
fields.prompt: Track reproducibility, citation accuracy, entity-match errors, counsel rejection, and confidentiality incidents using stable definitions. Keep research rejection separate from filed-case non-intervention or dismissal so small samples cannot imply government outcome rates.
fields.example: The pilot checks 100 material citations and finds two errors, yielding 98% initial accuracy and 100% after documented correction. Counsel rejects three of eight leads for insufficient corroboration. No complaints have been filed, so there is no observed DOJ outcome cohort to calculate.

fields.name: Client concentration and renewal resilience
fields.prompt: Measure client concentration, renewal dates, termination notice, receivable exposure, and delivery dependency. Describe the specific staffing and cash response if the largest retainer ends before replacement business is collected.
fields.example: At Base steady state, each of five equal retainers represents 20% of recurring fees. Losing one removes $7,500 monthly revenue. The operator reviews notice terms, reduces uncommitted contractor hours, and uses the unrestricted reserve while replacing the account. They do not bridge the gap with projected awards.

fields.name: Exit-readiness assets and transfer restrictions
fields.prompt: Inventory owned code, documentation, licensed sources, contracts, client permissions, and restricted evidence. Identify assignment conditions and counsel review before any buyer receives materials or an award interest appears in a sale schedule.
fields.example: The asset register lists parser code, test fixtures, and generic operating procedures as operator-owned. Two dataset licenses require vendor approval for transfer; five service contracts require assignment review. Restricted client evidence stays outside the initial buyer room. Contingent statutory interests are excluded pending specific counsel analysis.

fields.name: Owner decision and canonical benchmark ledger
fields.prompt: Record the owner's continue, narrow, or pause decision against actual cash, quality, capacity, and buyer evidence. Retain the canonical score and scenario benchmarks without presenting them as achieved results.
fields.example: The decision ledger retains pipeline rank #16 of 49 and score 92/100, comprising 24 revenue, 24 margin, 20 team, 12 accessibility, and 12 automation points. Annual profit benchmarks remain $30,400, $219,375, and $510,400. The owner continues a cash-capped launch; none of those benchmarks is reported as earned.

worksheets.completion_gate: Close the sprint when all six worksheets have accountable owners, cash and quality metrics reconcile to evidence, the next month's spend is funded without awards, and transfer restrictions are recorded before any external diligence.
